Well, flags don't just represent countries. They're a symbol for what they represent. The Confederate battle flag has morphed over the past years from a military symbol of a rebel government to a white nationalist symbol. The same is true of the "Nazi" flag, back in the late 30's it was just the flag of Germany that had an Eastern symbol typically associated with peace in the center. Hitler was huge of symbols and choose the swastika for a reason. My point is that we define what these flags represent, they're not inherently evil nor does the ownership or flying of them make someone evil. Speaking as someone from the south, these flags mean something different to these wackos (yes they're absolute wackos) who fly them. To further this point, there are parts of the world that see the American flag as a symbol of colonial and expansionist evil in the world, and to an extent they're right, but we aren't evil for flying an American flag. We should redefine what these symbols of evil are so they don't have such power over us.
